newsitem.title: USA: Indiana fast planting pace continues, growth slow.
newsitem.headline: Indiana fast planting pace continues, growth slow.

text.p: Indiana's spring planting continued to stay far ahead of average in the week ended May 18 but cool weather also kept germination slow, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.
"Many farmers are finished planting corn. Emergence has been very slow due to cool temperatures and some soil crusting. Some fields are being evaluated for potential replanting," the agency said.
Corn planted 86 percent vs 71 week ago, 13 year ago, 57 on a five-year average.
Soybeans planted 54 pct vs 31 w/a, 4 y/a, 28 avge.
Winter wheat jointed 97 pct vs 89 w/a, 86 y/a, 89 avge.
Winter wheat headed 30 pct vs 10 w/a, 21 y/a, 27 avge.
Winter wheat conditions was rated 69 percent good to excellent vs 62 percent last week, with 27 percent rated fair and 4 percent rated poor.
Pastures were rated 68 percent good to excellent, 31 fair.
Topsoil moisture was rated 86 percent surplus to adequate, versus 97 percent a week ago. Subsoil mositure was rated 95 percent surplus to adequate, versus 97 percent last week.
